newsitem.title: USA: House panel plans more subpoenas on campaign funds.
newsitem.headline: House panel plans more subpoenas on campaign funds.

text.p: The head of a House panel investigating allegations of illegal fund raising by the White House vowed on Saturday to get to the bottom of the mounting controversy and said he would soon issue more subpoenas.

House Government Reform and Oversight Committee Chairman Dan Burton told CNN's "Evans & Novak" programme he hoped his investigations would not point to an impeachable offence by President Bill Clinton.
"I quite frankly would hope that it would not come to that. I think it would be tragic for the country to have another problem like we had with Watergate," the Indiana Republican told CNN.

"I would hope the president is not guilty of anything like that," he said. "If we get to the point where we find information like that, of course we'll have to take the proper actions. But I hope it never comes to that."

Representative Bobb Barr, a George Republican, on Friday said he had asked the House Judiciary Committee to hold a meeting to discuss whether campaign fundraising activities by Clinton and Vice President Al Gore warranted impeachment proceedings.
Under the impeachment process, the House Judiciary Committee would have to conduct an investigation and then vote on whether to impeach Clinton and Gore.

If the panel approved one or more articles of impeachment and the full House adopted them, a trial would be held with members of the Senate as the jury. A two-thirds majority of the 100 senators is needed to remove an impeached official.

The last time the impeachment process was used against a president was in 1974 when the Judiciary Committee approved articles of impeachment against Richard Nixon. He resigned before the full House could vote on them.

"We're going to be very diligent. We're going to be very fair but very thorough in getting to the bottom of this,": Burton said. "I think it's important for the country. I think it's important for the presidency and I think it's important to show that the Congress is doing it's job."
He said further subpoenas would be issued "in the not too distant future", probably over the next three or four weeks.

The Justice Department is investigating reports of improper fundraising which include allegations the Chinese may have funnelled money illegally into U.S. campaigns, and Republicans are pressuring Attorney General Janet Reno to recommend appointment of an independent prosecutor.

Discussion of possible impeachment proceedings underscored "the seriousness and the gravity of this scandal that seems to burgeon every day," Republican National Committee Chairman Jim Nicholson told CNN's "Inside Politcs Weekend".

"What needs to happen right now is that we need to get to the bottom of all this, which is why the attorney general should appoint an independent counsel so that ... we can establish exactly what the facts are."

Burton raised questions about an exchange between the FBI and White House national security officials over intelligence reports that the Chinese government planned to contribute heavily to congressional and presidential campaigns. The officials said the FBI told them not to pass the information on to the president, but FBI says it never said that.
Burton said his panel had subpoenaed documents from the White House and the Justice Department, and said interviews with key officials involved in the briefing were likely.
"The Chinese Embassy and the electronic surveillance would indicate they were trying to buy influence and trying to influence the foreign policy of the United States," he said.

The committee was also looking into reports a Chinese firm owned in part by the Chinese Liberation Army built a shipping base in California, focusing on "how that affects our foreign policy and whether or not that's an intelligence threat."
Burton said Clinton had conversations about the agreement establishing the base in 1995 and 1996 and was "very adamant and very aggressive in pushing this project forward."

"It probably should be reviewed thoroughly from the standpoint of national security, and we also need to look at it from the standpoint of whether or not there were any illegal contributions that had something to do with the final outcome," he said.
